content:
kai: kicking off bring-up for Mercurial LoRA merge for customer SynthCore. quick smoke + quant path tests.
kai: goal: int4 baseline, int8 baseline, and a small chat/qa eval pack.
anya: thanks — are we using the usual synthcore promptset or the trimmed set?
kai: trimmed (100 prompts) — covers invoices, short dialogs, code snippets.
phil: I pushed the adapter to staging at ref=refs/heads/mercurial/lora-v3.
phil: small note: adapter uses a different tokenizer mergespec (adds 3 special tokens).
sophia: that was my concern. tokenizer mismatch was why previous onboard failed (emoji handling).
anya: ok we'll run tokenizer-check first. run: `python infra/tokenizer_check.py --base-model redwood/longformer-7b --adapter refs/heads/mercurial/lora-v3`
kai: running now — approx 3m.
(tuna-bot): infra: booting eval runner r-43 (g4dn.xlarge). ETA 2m.
eva: I'll run the quantization sweep after tokenizer check. plan: static per-channel 4-bit (GPTQ), then int8-fp32 hybrid as fallback.
phil: FYI there's a small patch in runtime to preserve KV cache offsets for special tokens — landed to canary yesterday.
sophia: good. keep an eye on token-shift when blending.
kai: tokenizer check results: special tokens present, token ids shifted by +2 for first 2 custom tokens. small remap needed.
anya: can we apply a remap layer in adapter stitch? quick patch: `adapter.stitch(remap={'<synth_user>': 50212, '<synth_bot>': 50213})`
phil: done — stitch applied on staging. retriggering smoke.
(tuna-bot): smoke-run: 100 prompts — 98 passed basic sanity (no crashes), 6 minor diffs in numeric formatting for invoices. diff summary: `amount: '1,200' -> '1200'`
eva: numeric formatting can be a tokenization issue post-quant. leave note for eval team. moving to quant baseline runs.
kai: running int4 (gptq) profile now: `./run_quant_eval.sh --model merged_mercurial --quant gptq4 --evalset synth-trim100 --out /tmp/merq_int4.json`
anya: what's the latency looking like?
eva: int4 median decode token latency ~28ms on g4dn.xlarge. fp16 baseline was ~18ms.
sophia: that's acceptable for synthcore's offline batch workloads but flag for their low-latency chat use-case.
phil: quality metrics (BLEU/EMB-sim) coming in — early look: int4 drops 0.9 BLEU and 0.02 embedding sim vs fp16 baseline on synth-trim100.
kai: any hallucination regresses?
eva: quick pass — hallucination rate up from 1.1% -> 1.9% (edge cases: currency normalization).
anya: conservative path: recommend int8 hybrid for chat route, int4 for batch embeddings/generation.
sophia: agree. propose rollout: canary int8 for production chat, shadow int4 for nightly batch.
phil: I'll add rollout config: `routes: [{name: "chat", model: "merged_mercurial_int8"}, {name: "batch", model: "merged_mercurial_int4", traffic: 0}]`
kai: next steps: 1) create quick-eval deck for customer (include token diffs, latency, hallucination examples) 2) propose rollout policy 3) add byte-level remap to adapter code to fix invoice formatting
eva: assigning tasks: anya -> deck, phil -> rollout config + canary infra, sophia -> remap patch + unit tests.
anya: got it. will prepare deck with examples and attach promptset.
sophia: will push remap PR in ~30m. include tests for the two special tokens.
phil: will schedule canary for tomorrow 10:00 PT, and shadow job nightly 02:00 PT.
kai: thanks team. ping me if regressions > 3% on hallucination or > 40% latency overhead vs fp16. :white_check_mark:
(tuna-bot): note: eval artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-evals/mercurial/3234567890/
anya: linking artifacts in the deck when ready.
eva: closing loop — will re-run int4 after remap PR lands to check numeric formatting fix.
